newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coffee prices hit German roaster's profits.
newsitem.headline: Coffee prices hit German roaster's profits.

text.p: High green coffee prices in the world market and retail price competition more than halved 1995 operating profits at Germany's Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), the company said on Tuesday.
A KJS statement said profits in 1995 of 188 million marks compared with 452 million in 1994 while turnover eased to 4.6 billion marks (4.7 billion in 1994).
Restructuring measures in response to the profit decline were adding to 1996 operating costs so that a significantly higher result this year could be ruled out.
The coffee, confectionery and food products company, which is part of U.S. group Philip Morris, is the market leader in roasted coffee and solid chocolate bars.
Restructuring included centralisation of sales efforts and the creation of larger production units.
